title: 完整的小院圆舞曲  (Courtyard Waltz Complete)

segments.t: Six o'clock arrives in Chengdu. Inside the warm glow of Room Nine, Teacher Song stands beside the walnut upright piano while Manager Zhou, Qing, and two dozen neighbours listen through the open green shutters. Listen first.
朋友们晚上好，欢迎回到九号房的星期五晚茶。
三十年前的五月，我姑姑就在这架钢琴前写下了一首小圆舞曲。
大雨打断了第二页——直到小晴和老陈重新推开这几扇窗板。
今晚，十号院的邻居还用小提琴跟宋老师一起合奏！
老朋友，数到三就开始？一、二、三……
周经理，听钢琴弹到中央瑞音的时候，小提琴飞得多高！
连我的眼镜都起雾了——而且这一回我知道它在哪儿！
快看外面：走在梧桐巷上的路人，都停在大门口听了！
最后一个温柔的和弦，高一个八度——又回家了。
好极了！太棒了，宋老师！您听全院子的掌声！
周经理，您自己也鞠个躬吧——您姑姑的星期五茶室又活过来了。
谁也舍不得回家呢——该上肉桂卷啦！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
朋友们晚上好，欢迎回到九号房的星期五晚茶。

'Good evening, friends, and welcome back to Friday tea in Room Nine.' Teacher Song greets the whole courtyard with "wanshang hao", "good evening", and "huanying huidao"—"welcome back to"—as if thirty years had barely passed.
三十年前的五月，我姑姑就在这架钢琴前写下了一首小圆舞曲。

'Thirty years ago in May, my aunt started a little waltz right at this piano.' A piano takes the frame-counter "jia", a song takes "shou", and "yuanwuqu" paints a waltz in three strokes: "round-dance-tune".
大雨打断了第二页——直到小晴和老陈重新推开这几扇窗板。

'Rain interrupted page two—until Qing and Chen pushed these shutters open again.' "Daduan", literally "strike broken", is the everyday word for interrupting music or speech, while doors, windows, and shutters all take the fan-shaped counter "shan".
今晚，十号院的邻居还用小提琴跟宋老师一起合奏！

'And tonight, our neighbour from number ten joins Teacher Song on the violin!' "Hezou" joins "together" with "perform music", giving Mandarin a single poised word for playing an instrumental duet or ensemble.
老朋友，数到三就开始？一、二、三……
'Ready on three, my friend? One, two, three...' "Shu dao san jiu kaishi"—"count to three then start"—is how musicians and photographers cue a group in Mandarin.
周经理，听钢琴弹到中央瑞音的时候，小提琴飞得多高！

'Listen to how high the violin soars when the piano reaches middle D, Manager Zhou!' Notice "duo gao!" at the end: in exclamations, "duo" doesn't mean "many"—it means "how high!", just like "how lovely!".
连我的眼镜都起雾了——而且这一回我知道它在哪儿！

'Even my glasses are misty—and for once I know right where they are!' "Lian... dou" spotlights a surprising extreme—"even my glasses!"—and two-syllable "qiwu" literally says "rise fog" when lenses steam up.
快看外面：走在梧桐巷上的路人，都停在大门口听了！
'Look outside: people walking down Wutong Lane have stopped by the gate to listen!' "Luren" couldn't be simpler to remember: "road" plus "person" gives you "passer-by".
最后一个温柔的和弦，高一个八度——又回家了。

'And there is our gentle final chord, one octave high—home again.' "Hexian" pictures a musical chord as "harmonious strings" sounding together, and "badu", "eight degrees", matches English "octave" step for step.
好极了！太棒了，宋老师！您听全院子的掌声！

'Bravo! Bravo, Teacher Song! Hear the whole courtyard clapping!' The exclamation "hao ji le!"—"good to the utmost!"—is what you shout for "Bravo!" at a concert, and "zhangsheng" literally means "palm-sound".
周经理，您自己也鞠个躬吧——您姑姑的星期五茶室又活过来了。

'Take a bow yourself, Manager Zhou—your aunt's Friday room is alive again.' "Huo guolai", literally "live back over to our side", is the vivid everyday phrase for anything reviving—from a watered plant to an old music room.
谁也舍不得回家呢——该上肉桂卷啦！

'And nobody wants to go home yet—time for the cinnamon rolls!' Wait—notice how "shui ye" plus a negative turns "who" into "nobody at all", and "shebude" captures that warm reluctance when nobody wants a good evening to end.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
朋友们晚上好，欢迎回到九号房的星期五晚茶。
三十年前的五月，我姑姑就在这架钢琴前写下了一首小圆舞曲。
大雨打断了第二页——直到小晴和老陈重新推开这几扇窗板。
今晚，十号院的邻居还用小提琴跟宋老师一起合奏！
老朋友，数到三就开始？一、二、三……
周经理，听钢琴弹到中央瑞音的时候，小提琴飞得多高！
连我的眼镜都起雾了——而且这一回我知道它在哪儿！
快看外面：走在梧桐巷上的路人，都停在大门口听了！
最后一个温柔的和弦，高一个八度——又回家了。
好极了！太棒了，宋老师！您听全院子的掌声！
周经理，您自己也鞠个躬吧——您姑姑的星期五茶室又活过来了。
谁也舍不得回家呢——该上肉桂卷啦！
Piano and violin carry the finished "Courtyard Waltz" out into the warm Friday night to heartfelt applause. See you next time.
再见！
